title: No chips, no power: Africa and the semiconductor value chain

recommendations.text: Enter the semiconductor value chain through feasible segments: chip design, assembly, testing and packaging, and power electronics.
recommendations.why: Fabrication needs capital, infrastructure and reliable energy that Africa lacks today; these segments need far less.
No single African market is large enough on its own.

recommendations.text: Link Africa’s critical minerals to chip-related production rather than exporting them raw.
recommendations.why: Africa holds a large share of the minerals used in chips but contributes less than 1% of global semiconductor output.

issue: Chips run everything from cars to clinics to the power grid. Africa supplies many of the critical minerals used to make them, but accounts for less than 1% of global semiconductor output.
evidence: Fabrication is highly capital-intensive and needs advanced infrastructure, industrial water and reliable power. Chip design does not require a fabrication plant, and assembly, testing and packaging need much lower investment. Countries such as Morocco, Nigeria, Kenya and Rwanda are already moving into these segments.
